findings.category: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: 402/407/408 status is discarded — a permanent hold becomes undiagnosable, and the operator is told to do nothing
findings.description:
The new classification builds `ClaudeOutageError(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")`, but on the outage path that message is never emitted anywhere. Traced every sink: (1) news_bot.py:3165 logs `[hold] LLM outage for {link} — holding article...` with NO exception text; (2) `outage_state.record_outage_event(now)` takes only a timestamp; (3) the pings it returns are 100% static builders (`admin_alerts.alert_outage_first_ping` / `_second_ping` / `_still_down`, admin_alerts.py:496-532) — no interpolation of exception data; (4) `_publish_with_retries` (news_bot.py:3665) returns `('held', None)`, dropping the exception object, so no `last_error` is written and the [E034] recap is not touched; (5) the engine itself never logs the exception — openrouter_transcreation.py:444 goes straight `except openai.OpenAIError as exc: raise _classify_exception(exc)`.

This is security-positive for the leak question (see the note in the summary) but it is a real detection regression. BEFORE the change, a 402 travelled the per-article path, so `sanitize_error_message(exc)` put «Insufficient credits» into the WARNING at news_bot.py:3154 and into the sanitized [E034] publish recap plus `failed_articles.last_error`. AFTER the change, that text exists nowhere. The only operator signal is [E010]/[E011]/[E012], whose wording is factually wrong for 402: «Claude API недоступна… Что сделать: ничего — посты придержаны и выйдут автоматически» and «глянь статус api.anthropic.com». A 402 never self-heals — it needs a top-up — and prod runs OpenRouter, not Anthropic, so the ping points the operator at the wrong dashboard. After ping #3 (2h) `_compute_next_state` returns `({}, [], True, 'google_fallback_active')` for `ping_count >= 3`: no further pings, ever.
findings.impact: The exact incident this change was written for (2026-07-14, OpenRouter out of credits) now produces a stopped channel with three misleading pings and then permanent silence. Root-causing it requires the operator to open the OpenRouter console by hand — the bot's own logs and admin chat contain no evidence of which status code caused the hold, so 402 (needs money), 407 (needs proxy fix) and 429/5xx (genuinely self-healing) are indistinguishable. Mean time to recovery goes up on precisely the failure class that cannot recover on its own.
findings.recommendation:
Keep the Decision-12 invariant (never `str(exc)` in a user-visible ping) but restore the status code, which is not secret-bearing:

```python
# news_bot.py, in `except ClaudeOutageError as exc:`
status = getattr(exc, 'status_code', None) or _status_from_message(exc)
logger.warning(
    f"[hold] LLM outage for {link} (status={status}) — holding article..."
)
```
To carry the code across the boundary cleanly, attach it in the classifier instead of parsing it back out:
```python
# _llm_common.py
class ClaudeOutageError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, *, status_code=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status_code = status_code
# each engine:
if _is_account_level_status(exc):
    return ClaudeOutageError(
        f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", status_code=exc.status_code
    )
```
Then branch the ping: 402 deserves its own actionable alert (e.g. `[E0xx] 🔴 Кончились кредиты — пополни баланс, посты придержаны`) rather than [E010]'s «ничего не делай». This also fixes the pre-existing wording bug where every outage blames «Claude API» regardless of the active engine.

findings.title: Unbounded head-of-queue hold now reachable via a request-cost-dependent 402, with no escalation and no cap
findings.description:
Answering the availability question directly: a hold is unbounded in time and unbounded in retries. `job()` re-reads `list_pending()[0]` every slot (news_bot.py:4391-4418), 'held' does not strike, and there is no max-hold age. The change widens the set of triggers to include 402, which — on OpenRouter specifically — is NOT purely account-global. OpenRouter returns 402 both for a zero balance AND per-request («This request requires more credits, or fewer max_tokens. You requested up to N tokens, but can only afford M»). Request cost = prompt tokens + the `max_tokens` reservation. `max_tokens` is a constant 30000 (openrouter_transcreation.py:76), so the reservation is uniform, but the prompt half is not: `_build_user_message` (_llm_common.py:246-285) serialises every paragraph of the article with NO cap on paragraph count or total payload size (the only cap, `_PARAGRAPH_MAX_CHARS = 4000`, is applied to the RESPONSE via `_truncate_paragraphs`, not to the request). A long round-up therefore costs measurably more than a short news item.

Consequence: with a balance in the band between the two costs, a long article at the queue head 402s on every slot forever, while the shorter articles queued behind it would have succeeded. The 3-strike escape hatch that used to drain that row is now gone by design.

Assessment of the specific codes, so severity is not overstated:
- 402 — the real content-correlated case above. Narrow band, and partially mitigated (below).
- 408 — size/latency correlated in principle, but a 60s client-side timeout (`timeout_s: int = 60`) fires first as `APITimeoutError`, which was ALREADY classified as an outage before this change. Both openai and anthropic SDKs also auto-retry 408 internally. So 408 adds nothing qualitatively new to the wedge surface.
- 407 — no proxy is configured anywhere (Dockerfile / docker-compose.yml / .env.example / deploy.sh contain no proxy vars); prod egress is a VPN, not an HTTP proxy. Not article-inducible.
- Article CONTENT (prompt injection in a source body) cannot produce any of the three: the status is chosen by the gateway before the model sees the text.

Existing mitigating controls, all partial: `_maybe_alert_openrouter_balance` pings [E019] below $5 (OpenRouter only — no equivalent probe for the openai or claude engines, and it is best-effort/swallowing); the daily [E008] plan-of-day carries the pending count so a growing backlog is visible; the external GitHub-Actions watchdog checks the last Telegra.ph page date. None of them bound the hold.
findings.impact: A single head-of-queue article can stop the entire channel indefinitely on a condition the bot cannot resolve by itself, with no further alerts after the 2h mark. Cost side-effect: each held slot re-issues the full 30k-max_tokens request for the same article (3 slots/day, forever), where the old path capped it at 3 attempts total — an unbounded spend loop on a persistently-rejected request.
findings.recommendation:
Bound the hold. Minimal version — track consecutive holds per link and escalate rather than loop silently:

```python
# after N consecutive held slots on the SAME link
if held_link == row['link'] and held_streak >= MAX_HELD_SLOTS:
    send_admin_notification(admin_alerts.alert_article_stuck_held(link, held_streak))
    # and either strike, or rotate to rows[1] so the rest of the queue drains
```
Rotating past the stuck row is the stronger fix for the 402 band case specifically, because the shorter articles behind it are affordable. At minimum, re-emit an outage ping every 24h while a hold is active instead of going silent at `ping_count >= 3`, and consider capping request payload size (paragraph count) in `_build_user_message` so per-request cost stops tracking upstream article length.

findings.title: Retained per-article default for 413/451 has a silent mass-drop mode when the cause is global
findings.description:
Answering question 3: the retained default introduces no NEW exposure — 413/451 keep the exact pre-change path (`ClaudeTranscreationError` → strike → `sanitize_error_message` into `last_error` and the [E034] recap → `send_admin_notification` → `_redact_text`). That path is double-redacted and unchanged.

The residual concern is a design one the diff canonicalises in a comment: 413 «payload too large» is framed as «about THIS article», but the request also carries the shared system prompt (`_build_system_prompt` = the full `ux-guidelines.md` body + JSON envelope), which is operator-editable and has grown over time (memory note: «не сокращать промпт перевода ради токенов»). If a prompt edit or a gateway limit change makes EVERY request exceed a limit, 413 becomes global while still being classified per-article — and the 3-strike machine will silently drain the entire pending queue into `failed_articles`, three attempts per row, with no outage ping. 451 has the same shape if a provider geo-blocks the egress IP wholesale.
findings.impact: A global failure misread as per-article destroys the queue instead of holding it: every pending article is struck out and moved to `failed_articles`. Recovery requires manual re-staging of each row. The failure is loud in the [E034] recap but is not distinguished from ordinary article-quality strikes, so it can run for a full day before anyone notices the pattern.
findings.recommendation:
The 402/413 split is the right call — do not widen the outage set. Instead add a consecutive-failure circuit breaker so a global problem cannot masquerade as N independent article problems:

```python
# in job(), around the 'failed' branch
if same_status_streak >= CONSECUTIVE_SAME_STATUS_LIMIT:  # e.g. 3
    send_admin_notification(admin_alerts.alert_systemic_llm_rejection(status, streak))
    break  # stop striking; leave the rest of the queue intact
```
This is the generic guard that makes the per-article default safe to keep as the catch-all for genuinely novel codes.

findings.title: Proxy credentials are outside the redaction vocabulary, while the change explicitly anticipates an egress proxy
findings.description:
The new `_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES` documents 407 as «the egress proxy, not the article», i.e. the design anticipates a proxy in front of the LLM egress. No proxy is configured today (verified: no proxy env in Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example or deploy.sh — prod egress is a VPN), so this is latent, not live.

If an operator later sets `HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:pass@host`, that credential is covered by NOTHING in the three-layer defence: `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES` (news_bot.py:229-239) has no `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` entry, and none of the five `_redact_text` regexes (`_BOT_TOKEN_RE`, `_OPENROUTER_KEY_RE`, `_ANTHROPIC_KEY_RE`, `_OPENAI_KEY_RE`, `_GEMINI_KEY_RE`) match a `scheme://user:pass@host` shape. httpx and both SDKs can embed the proxy URL in connection-error strings, which reach logs through paths that log full exception text (e.g. openrouter_transcreation.py:543 `logger.info("health_check: probe failed: %s: %s", type(exc).__name__, exc)`).

Note this is NOT reachable through the new 402/407/408 path itself: an `APIStatusError` message is `Error code: 407 - <response body>` — a proxy's auth challenge body and `Proxy-Authenticate` header carry no client credentials, and per the first finding the message is never emitted anyway. The gap is in the surrounding redaction vocabulary, exposed by the fact that the change now names a proxy as a supported topology.
findings.impact: If a proxy with inline credentials is ever configured, its username and password can be written verbatim to the container logs (`docker logs hw-news-bot`) via any dependency's connection-error string, and would survive both redaction layers. Anyone with log access — including the log-shipping path — obtains working egress credentials.
findings.recommendation:
Close it now, while it costs one line each. Add `'HTTP_PROXY', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'ALL_PROXY'` (and lowercase variants) to `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES`, and add a URL-credential pattern to `_redact_text`, placed anywhere in the chain since it cannot collide with the `sk-` patterns:

```python
_URL_CREDS_RE = re.compile(r"://[^/\s:@]+:[^/\s@]+@")
# in _redact_text:
text = _URL_CREDS_RE.sub("://***:***@", text)
```
Per patterns.md the pattern list is a documented contract — adding one means updating the order note in the `_redact_text` docstring too.

findings.title: requests==2.32.3 is affected by CVE-2024-47081 (.netrc credential leak via crafted URL)
findings.description: PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to this diff — reported because dependency scanning is a mandatory check. `requirements.txt` pins `requests==2.32.3`; CVE-2024-47081 (fixed in 2.32.4) lets a maliciously-crafted URL cause `requests` to leak `.netrc` credentials to an unintended host. The bot fetches URLs that originate in RSS entries (`fetch_rss`, and `fetch_mattel_article`, which patterns.md:372 already flags as «reachable from external link»), so the attacker-influenced-URL precondition is satisfiable by a compromised or hostile source feed. Exploitability is low in practice: the container image is not expected to contain a `.netrc`, which is the only credential store the CVE reads. Other pinned deps are clean at the versions installed (anthropic 0.45.2, openai 2.32.0, httpx 0.28.1, urllib3 2.6.3, python-telegram-bot 21.10, feedparser 6.0.12); the diff adds no new dependency — `httpx` in the two test files is already a transitive dep of `openai`.
findings.impact: With a `.netrc` present in the runtime image, a hostile RSS entry URL that redirects cross-host could exfiltrate stored credentials to the attacker's host. Without a `.netrc` — the expected state here — impact is nil, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.recommendation: Bump on the next dependency pass: `requests==2.32.4` (patch release, no API change). Confirm no `.netrc` is baked into the image while you are there.
